questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
questions.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-6\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6{\text{i}}^{2} \\ \text{i}-2{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3-8\text{i} \\ -4+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-8\text{i} \\ -2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4+3\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4+3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1+3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5+4\text{i} \\ -4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ -4\text{i}-3{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+5\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4+5\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 2-7\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the real part of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ -4+7\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}c \\ d\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} \\ -1-5\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ac+bd?$
questions.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} \\ -1-5\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}1-3\text{i} \\ -1-5\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $\,a=1,b=-1,c=-3$ and $d=-5$, which implies that 

$$
ac+bd=1\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot (-5)=2.
$$

$$

So, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}4\overset{―}{k}=-20+28\text{i} \\ (-5+\text{i})\overset{―}{k}=18-40\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get

$$
\overset{―}{k}=-5+7\text{i}

$$
(-5+\text{i})(-5+7\text{i})=18-40\text{i}

$$

$$
3\text{i}\,\overset{―}{k}=3\text{i}-9\,⟹\,\overset{―}{k}=\frac{3\text{i}-9}{3\text{i}}=1+3\text{i}.

$$

$$
